name: Washington D.C.
limitations: All 31 subpillars are reviewed, not all are measured. Scores require the stated assumptions; unknown evidence remains unknown. This is neither a global ranking nor an exclusion bound. Rejecting a necessary assumption requires reassessment, not automatic retention of its score.

dimensions.rationale: An actually activated June 2026 heat alert, existing cooling sites and accessible transport support protection. Whole-FUA reach, health-loss reduction, other hazards and outage operation remain unverified.
dimensions.assumption: Observed protection usually works, persists and applies across the functional area without broader unmitigated failure from unreviewed hazards; rejecting these assumptions leaves PCS unresolved.

dimensions.rationale: Dated court records and Justice Department notices describe the May 2025 museum attack with two deaths and the November 2025 Guard attack with one death and one critically injured person, together with actual police, emergency and on-scene responses. They are selected incidents, not annual whole-FUA rates or proof of organised-group membership; charges and prosecutor accounts are not convictions. Their local effects do not yet establish the broader regional or strategic impact profile required for an anchor.
dimensions.assumption: No justified whole-dimension anchor yet. Actual incident response supports mitigation but neither a small selected incident set nor preliminary ordinary-crime counts establishes low overall resident impact. Whole-area, temporal and broader threat effects remain unresolved.

dimensions.rationale: Delivered heat, food-access and digital services and operating complaints oversight support execution. An audit of complaint-related police stop reports identifies missing mandated fields; MPD describes alternative customised records. Neither transparent disclosure nor incomplete stock fields establish whole-area institutional failure.
dimensions.assumption: Observed execution persists and major services usually operate; the reviewed historical documentation defect has not become a broader unmitigated institutional bottleneck. Rejecting temporal, resident or boundary applicability leaves ISR unresolved.

dimensions.rationale: A 2026 probability-based regional survey reports food insecurity in approximately one quarter of middle-income households, defined by income thirds. Actual food-access help and ordinary water operations do not establish that this material resource constraint is relieved. The survey does not specifically measure median-income citizens or the frozen FUA.
dimensions.assumption: The surveyed middle-income household experience applies to ordinary local citizens across the FUA and persists through the cutoff as an important insufficiently relieved basic-resource constraint. Rejecting representativeness or continuity leaves RES unresolved; verified relief plus usual other supplies can justify reassessment to 60, not an automatic upgrade.

dimensions.rationale: A dated local 2024 report describes an operating hypertension telehealth clinic with in-person links and observed benefits, alongside device and assistance barriers. A Spring 2026 provider report documents actual Washington LVAD implantations, strengthening specialist delivery evidence but not whole-FUA outcomes or median-resident affordability. Current emergency pages and national insurance limits remain conditional context; routine quality, waits and crisis continuity are unverified.
dimensions.assumption: Historical actual services persist and necessary treatment is usually obtainable, clinically adequate and affordable under usual coverage for the target resident. Undated pages and national insurance rules do not establish these conditions; rejecting them leaves MED unresolved.

dimensions.rationale: A credible early-Alzheimer confirmatory trial and FDA approval now connect to actual 2024 Medicare FFS lecanemab claims for a provider whose end-following-year NPPES address matches the dated Sterling clinic opening. The address-range point intersects the frozen FUA; claims are not treatment-site or patient-residence coordinates. Dated referral, insurance and 2025 network delivery records support a limited adoption pathway. Eligibility, coinsurance, referral/MRI logistics and serious ARIA risk remain constraints; the 2024 referral form predates the 2025 FDA safety update. No local clinical outcome or healthy-person lifespan gain is established.
dimensions.assumption: The selected historical claims represent delivery within the functional area, the limited disease-specific pathway is relevant to LON readiness, and actual services and appropriate current safety monitoring persist through the cutoff. An ordinarily insured, clinically eligible local median-income citizen can usually obtain and afford diagnosis, referral, treatment and follow-up across the FUA; citizenship, listed insurance and observed Medicare beneficiaries do not establish these conditions. Rejecting location, continuity, pathway representativeness, monitoring or ordinary access restores LON to unresolved; verified important unrelieved barriers can justify 40, not source absence alone.

dimensions.rationale: Actual FY2025 GW sponsored research, patents and licensing alongside delivered digital workshops and outdoor Wi-Fi support output, industry links and partial diffusion. One university does not measure whole-FUA production; federal dependence and the June 2025 departure of a programme supplier remain counterevidence. Workshops and hotspots are not adoption rates.
dimensions.assumption: Observed research and digital capabilities persist and support limited industry connections and resident diffusion across the target area. Rejecting continuity or applicability leaves TEC unresolved; strong broad adoption and independent critical nodes are still needed for 80.

dimensions.rationale: Actual 2025 airport traffic and Silver Line airport-station trips support transport and ground access. The shared German section 41 application route, effective personal international-wire services and the January 2026 local outage/restoration notice support multiple conditional exit and connection paths. Residence approval, account approval and product restrictions, exchange spreads, disrupted 911 calls and shared failures are retained. Provider terms are not proof of a local resident completing a transfer; suggested alternatives are not measured universal backup.
dimensions.assumption: Observed channels and dated source versions remain applicable through the cutoff and across the FUA, and the median-income local citizen can usually obtain and afford usable travel, a qualifying residence-purpose pathway, a wire-capable account with compliant funds and destination access, and an alternative means of emergency contact when needed. Citizenship and median income do not establish job offers, qualifications, permission, bank approval or backup access. Rejecting ordinary availability, affordability, temporal or boundary applicability restores OPT to unresolved, not an automatic 40 or retained 60.

Complaint and supporting affidavit, seven PDF pages; filed May 22 for May 21 event. May 22 is the court filing date, not a verified public-release day or pre-cutoff archive.

Dated primary release read through web search: November 26 DC attack, one death on November 27, one critically injured person and two responding majors. Allegations are attributed; direct download returned a bot challenge despite HTTP 200, so no content snapshot hash claimed.

Five-page indictment, read in full; charges November 26/27 events. DOJ January 9 release identifies its unsealing; PDF creation January 12 is metadata, not verified publication day or cutoff archive. State of Washington is the alleged origin, not the DC incident location.

One-page March 25 2025 meeting material attributes figures to WMATA as of February 27: Dulles station 3.23 million cumulative customer trips since November 2022 opening, not unique airport users. March 20 PDF metadata is not publication; exact public-release day/cutoff archive and full-FUA access unverified.

Effective November 18 2025 edition; cover and pp.9-11 reviewed, regular rail $2.25-$6.75 excluding surcharge/differentials and payment requirements. PDF metadata November 17 is not publication; no pre-cutoff archive or whole-resident affordability measured. Supersedes the unused May 2025 edition.

Primary operator page read through web tool: approved FY2027 budget retains rail/bus fares. December changes and modernisation funding are plans, not delivered redundancy. No raw download hash claimed.

Effective June 14 2026 personal-account edition, PDF pp.1-3,13,15 reviewed. Total Checking terms and international-wire fees with account approval, exchange spreads and intermediary costs; Secure Checking excludes outgoing wires. File metadata is not publication/cutoff archive. Neither every account nor every local citizen has this channel; no completed resident transfer, asset liquidation, approvals or crisis continuity inferred.

Primary consumer rule explanation last reviewed October 3 2024; qualifying remittances over $15 and provider-volume conditions. Rights and disclosures are not transfer approval, delivery, a capital-transfer ceiling or city performance. Read through web tool; direct download unavailable, no raw hash claimed.

Local final update at 11:14 PM relays Verizon restoration after some users could not reach 911, and recommends another carrier, landline or station. Provider-reported restoration is not independent universal verification; advice does not measure alternative access/use or local outage duration.

All three pages reviewed: national outage and investigation invitation, not final findings, a DC-specific duration/rate or zero injuries. Media-attributed national scale is not local measurement; March comment deadline does not establish current investigation status.

All published 2024 J0174 provider/HCPCS/place-of-service rows, no geographic filter. Static year-specific API, not latest alias. 254 distinct NPI records, all non-facility O, minimum 11 beneficiaries; not a patient-level file.
Pagination end check: offset 254 returns an empty array. This verifies the filtered published query, not unsuppressed claims or all treatment settings.

Attached data dictionary: J0174 is 1 mg; beneficiary count is distinct only within NPI/code/place-of-service, day count is beneficiary-days, address is NPPES, O is non-facility, not exact physical site.
The 2024 dataset attaches the March 2025 dictionary and methodology; do not relabel them as 2026 documents. Original CSV size 3,250,282,192 bytes.

All eight pages extracted; pp.3-6 reviewed. Final-action non-institutional Part B FFS claims; records with ten or fewer beneficiaries suppressed. NPPES demographics extracted at end of year following service year, implying end-2025 address for 2024 data under the stated rule, not a 2024 treatment coordinate. No Medicare Advantage, uninsured, other payers or hospital facility payments; no quality outcomes.
Page posted July 19, 2024, body announcement July 18: opened Sterling and Dulles centres. Sterling address matches the selected claims record, not proof each claim occurred there.

Three-page public blank template, first two pages read; version 08.22.24 is form version, not verified publication day. Referral, amyloid, eligibility, MRI and Medicare registry requirements; not completed patient records. Its MRI schedule predates the FDA August 2025 update and is not a current safety protocol.

One scanned page visually reviewed: insurance contracts as of 6.1.24, including Medicare, Sterling and Dulles addresses; list subject to change and verification, not lecanemab authorisation or affordability. As-of date is not publication day.

Posted June 24, 2025: provider reports delivering Leqembi, coordinating referrals, monitoring and benefit/prior-authorisation checks. Network statement, not Sterling patient outcomes or automatic coverage. Promotional efficacy wording is not used as independent trial evidence.
August 28, 2025 safety communication adds MRI before the third infusion and retains serious/fatal ARIA risk. National safety evidence, not local harm incidence or proof the clinic adopted the update.

Current Census benchmark 4 yields one interpolated address-range point, not a verified building centroid or historical treatment site. Point projected to ESRI:54009 intersects only frozen eFUA 7068; whole-area resident coverage remains unresolved.

legalMobilityReview.meaning: Conditional procedural application route only; no automatic long-term residence/work entitlement. OPT 60 also depends on transport, asset and communication evidence and explicitly withdrawable ordinary-access assumptions.

localLonClaimsReview.addressSnapshotRule: End of calendar year following reporting year per attached CMS methodology; address is not claim-site geography.
localLonClaimsReview.boundaryMethod: Existing cci_global_crosswalk.load with source checksum, always_xy EPSG:4326 to ESRI:54009, point intersects frozen polygon; shapely 2.1.2 and pyproj 3.7.2. One address point, not whole-FUA service coverage.
localLonClaimsReview.interpretation: Historical actual billed adoption signal with explicit site and resident-access assumptions; 49,100 is drug units, 67 is beneficiary-days, 13 is distinct beneficiaries within this record, not FUA residents or healthy-person longevity outcomes.
